name: io.github.Davincc77/mechacut
title: mechacut
description: Deterministic compute bench for agents: exact math, money, dates, hashes; a sha256 on every answer.

tools.name: chart_from_data
tools.description: Deterministic chart from records or CSV. Returns a Vega-Lite spec and/or a PNG. No LLM, nothing stored. Same request -> same sha256. Never reorders your data: bars/pies aggregate (sum) per category in first-appearance order; lines keep input order.

kind.description: bar, line, area, point, step, histogram, pie

y.description: value column; required unless kind is histogram

tools.name: reshape_json
tools.description: Reshape JSON with a declarative mapping (path, cast, default, required, each). Optional outputSchema gate: the output is validated and rejected with precise errors on violation. No LLM, nothing stored.

outputSchema.description: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) the output must satisfy

tools.name: validate_json
tools.description: Validate a payload against a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12). Returns valid or precise errors.

tools.name: json_repair
tools.description: Repair broken JSON text deterministically (markdown fences, BOM, smart/single quotes, comments, bare keys, trailing commas, Python literals, JSONL). Returns the parsed value + repairs applied. Free.

tools.name: json_diff
tools.description: Structural diff between two JSON values: sorted changes with RFC 6901 pointer paths (added/removed/changed). Free.

tools.name: json_patch
tools.description: Apply an RFC 6902 patch (add/remove/replace/move/copy/test) to a document; per-operation errors with the failing index. Free under 32 KB, x402 above.

tools.name: json_canonical
tools.description: Canonical JSON bytes: keys sorted, minified or pretty, exact sha256 of the emitted text. Free.

tools.name: csv_fix
tools.description: Dirty CSV -> clean comma-CSV with \n endings: BOM stripped, line endings unified, delimiter detected, blank rows removed, headers normalized (empty named, duplicates suffixed), short/long rows padded/truncated. Returns notes. Free under 32 KB, x402 above.

preserve_delimiter.description: keep the detected delimiter instead of comma

tools.name: csv_types
tools.description: Infer and coerce column types (int, float, bool, date, datetime, string, null) over CSV text or records; returns typed rows and a column report with null counts. Free under 32 KB, x402 above.

tools.name: csv_join
tools.description: Join two record tables (inner|left|right|outer) on a key column or [leftKey, rightKey]; overlapping columns: left wins; rows missing the key never match. Paid route (x402 from first call).

tools.name: table_pivot
tools.description: Pivot records (index x columns -> aggregated values, agg sum|count|mean|min|max|first, columns sorted, missing -> null) or unpivot (melt, keep/vars). Paid route (x402 from first call).

index.description: pivot: column or list of columns

tools.name: list_dedupe
tools.description: Dedupe a list keeping the first occurrence and the original values: modes exact | text (NFC, whitespace, casefold) | url (scheme/host case, default ports, trailing slash, fragment, sorted query) | email (lowercase local@domain). Free.

tools.name: format_convert
tools.description: Convert between json, yaml, toml, csv, env. Deterministic: keys sorted where the format allows, \n endings. env requires flat scalars; toml requires an object; csv requires an array of objects. Free under 32 KB, x402 above.

tools.name: text_patch
tools.description: Find/replace edits on a text, applied in order, each verified: 'occurrences' is "one" (default: exact-uniqueness gate), "all" or an exact count. A non-unique rename fails loudly instead of guessing. Paid route (x402 from first call).

tools.name: text_diff
tools.description: Unified line diff between two texts, fixed labels (before/after), configurable context (default 3), stats (hunks/added/removed), identical flag, exact sha256. Free under 32 KB, x402 above.

tools.name: text_apply_diff
tools.description: Apply a unified diff STRICTLY: every context and deletion line must match its documented position; mismatches name the hunk and line — no fuzz, no silent reflow. Paid route (x402).

tools.name: path_normalize
tools.description: Lexical path normalization to POSIX form (auto posix/windows, . and .. resolution never crossing root, optional lowercase) + name/stem/extension. Never touches the filesystem. Free.

tools.name: glob_match
tools.description: Deterministic glob over a list of paths: * and ? do not cross /, ** spans segments, dots are literal, case-sensitive, input order preserved. No filesystem. Free.

tools.name: env_interpolate
tools.description: Expand $VAR, ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} from a vars object. strict=true (default) fails naming every missing var; strict=false keeps them literal and reports `missing`. Free.

tools.name: date_parse
tools.description: Parse one date (ISO 8601, RFC 2822, epoch seconds, slashed numeric: 03/04/05-style is REFUSED with both readings named until prefer is given (13/04 and 05/05 answer — the bytes decide) — never guessed — or month-name form) -> ISO, UTC, epoch, weekday, ISO week, naive flag. Free.

tz.description: IANA zone to interpret a naive value in

tools.name: date_tz
tools.description: Convert an instant or bare date into IANA zones with correct DST: ISO output per zone, offset, dst flag. Naive inputs read in `source` (default UTC); bare dates get `at` (HH:MM, default 00:00). Free.

tools.name: date_calc
tools.description: Date arithmetic: add (calendar-aware duration like "1y2m3dT4h", month-end clamped), business_days (n, holidays, weekend), diff (days|business_days|human|calendar; business_days counts base-exclusive by default, include_base=true counts BOTH endpoints, backward windows with include_base are refused, not mirrored), boundary (day|week|month|quarter|year, start|end), age. Free.

tools.name: cron_next
tools.description: Next N fire times of a 5-field cron expression (or @macro), wall-clock semantics in `tz`, Vixie dom/dow OR rule. Pin `after` for a byte-stable answer. Free.

tools.name: cron_humanize
tools.description: Cron expression -> plain reading + resolved field sets. Free.

tools.name: ics_generate
tools.description: Events -> deterministic RFC 5545 VCALENDAR: CRLF, 75-octet folding, DTSTAMP mirrors DTSTART when absent so bytes never drift. Free under 32 KB, x402 above.

tools.name: ics_parse
tools.description: VCALENDAR -> calendar meta + normalized events (ISO starts/ends, duration seconds, RRULE raw passthrough, unescaped text). Free under 32 KB, x402 above.

tools.name: num_format
tools.description: Deterministic number/currency/percent formatting from CLOSED locale (13) and currency (20) tables, Decimal-based: 1234.567 -> "1,234.567", fr-FR EUR currency -> "1 234,57 €", "12.34%". Free.

tools.name: num_parse
tools.description: Human number -> canonical decimal_string + float + currency + percent flags. Handles grouping styles (1,234.56 / 1.234,56 / 1'234.56 / spaces), symbols and ISO codes. Ambiguity is REFUSED, not guessed: 1,234 needs prefer="decimal" or "group". Free.

tools.name: num_round
tools.description: Exact Decimal rounding: places 0-30 or significant digits, modes half_even (banker's, default) | half_up | half_down | ceil | floor | trunc | up. Same string in, same string out. Free.

tools.name: units_convert
tools.description: Unit conversion in closed families (length, mass, volume, area, speed, data incl. KiB/kbit distinction, duration, temperature) with exact rational factors - cross-family conversions are refused, unknown units name the table. Free.

tools.name: money_prorate
tools.description: Prorate a cycle amount over a service window: prorated = amount * covered_days / cycle_days, exact fraction reported, rounding is the last step (half_up default), window clamped to the cycle. Paid route (x402 from first call).

tools.name: money_aging
tools.description: Due-date aging of receivables: invoices (due ISO day, amount and optional paid as decimal strings) + mandatory as_of -> buckets 1-30/31-60/61-90/90+ (default [30,60,90], left-open right-closed on days_overdue), current, paid. The suite never reads a wall clock into a ledger. Overpaid invoice is a refusal, not a negative bucket. Free.

buckets.description: strictly increasing positive int day edges, default [30,60,90]

tools.name: money_split
tools.description: Split an amount to the cent with a CLOSED remainder rule: floor shares + leftover cents by fractional part, ties by list order - who gets the extra cent is deterministic. Equal or weighted participants. Free.

tools.name: number_spell
tools.description: Amount -> words for the invoice legal mention, in FR/EN/PT with closed grammatical rules (quatre-vingts, cent invariable before mille, duzentos/trezentos, e-rules) and currency unit naming. Same amount, same language, same words - forever. Free under 32 KB, x402 above.

currency.description: ISO code from the closed table

tools.name: id_ulid
tools.description: ULID make/parse/sort, Crockford base32, deterministic BY CONSTRUCTION: make demands timestamp_ms + entropy-hex or seed (same seed -> same id: retry-safe idempotency keys, no hidden clock). sort = chronological lexicographic. Free.

tools.name: pkg_name
tools.description: Package-name grammar verdict + normalization for npm (case/dot/charset), PyPI (PEP 503) and Docker (repo/tag/digest). Agents invent uppercase npm names and dotted tags; the registry will reject them — here they get told why, before the push. Free.

tools.name: net_ip
tools.description: IP address anatomy from the stdlib reference: v4/v6, private/loopback/link-local/multicast/reserved, reverse-DNS name, packed hex. Agents POST to 169.254.0.1 thinking it is routable; it is not, and now they can know. Free.

tools.name: net_cidr
tools.description: CIDR math: network/broadcast/prefix/usable hosts, contains(IP|subnet) verdict, split_into N-bit subnets (capped 256 listed). The cloud/infra agent chore done exactly. Free.

tools.name: file_encoding
tools.description: Charset forensics that never guesses: BOM table (5), strict utf-8 validation, and 'undetermined' with the exact failing byte offset + hex when the bytes do not prove a codec. The honest sibling of /text/decode. Free.

tools.name: schedule_overlap
tools.description: Interval arithmetic, four closed modes: merge (union + total), conflicts (overlapping pairs with seconds), free (gaps inside a window), contains (is this point busy?). No clock: every datetime is a caller argument. Free.

tools.name: cron_validate
tools.description: Vixie-cron semantics, five fields, names and steps accepted; descending ranges refused; 7 == 0 for Sunday; dom+dow both restricted ORs (documented footnote); calendar-impossible expressions get never + reason. Pass `at` to get the next runs — computed, not guessed. Free.

tools.name: integrity_verify
tools.description: Determinism Auditor: point it at any API with published pins (their integrity.json or an explicit pin list) and it re-plays every request N times over https, comparing sha256 — bytes mode (strictest) or json-canonical. Verdicts separate deterministic / non-deterministic / paywalled-(gate-stable) / unreachable. SSRF-guarded: https only, public IPs only (metadata ranges refused by name), hard fetch/byte/time caps. Paid $0.001: network egress is real work.

tools.name: math_calc
tools.description: The closed calculator — the model WRITES the expression, the machine COMPUTES it. Exact Decimal arithmetic from the SOURCE TEXT of every literal (0.1+0.2 = 0.3, never 0.30000000000000004): + - * / // % **, parentheses, unary sign, and exactly three named functions round(x[,n]) with declared HALF_UP, sqrt, abs. Everything else — names, letters, strings, attributes, lambdas, exponents over 64, divisions by zero, sqrt of negatives — REFUSED BY NAME, never silently clipped. digits=0..30 quantizes the final value and KEEPS trailing zeros (39.900 stays 39.900). 50-digit working precision declared in the answer. The engine under the formula catalogue to come. Free forever: arithmetic should cost nothing.

tools.name: money_discount
tools.description: The math the checkout will not do for you. '-30% then -20%' is NOT -50%: chained discounts are successive multiplicative factors (0.70 x 0.80 = 0.56 -> 44%), and the naive sum is reported SIDE BY SIDE with the lie's size (percent_lie_delta). When a fixed-amount step exists, ALL step orders are computed and compared: order_matters + order_spread + best_step_order_for_you — because -30%% then -5eur is not -5eur then -30%%. buy2pay1 with qty, exact Decimal money, final HALF_UP 2 dp declared, the formula returned for audit, below-zero chains refused by name never clipped. Free — this one should be free forever.

tools.name: formula_catalog
tools.description: The published-formula engine: 12 everyday formulas (rule of three, percent up/down with the round-trip gap named, speed/distance/time solved for any leg, fuel in BOTH senses, running pace, C1V1 dilution every target, mg/kg dosage with a scope note, baker's hydration 3 modes, Naegele EDD by two independent calendar paths, rational areas, cuboid volume, part-of-total share). The formula itself is in the answer, your numbers are substituted into it, the math is exact Fractions rendered to declared decimals. Zero constants in this palier by construction — pi and CODATA arrive with published digits. GET /api/v1/formula lists the closed catalog.

tools.name: intent_reflect
tools.description: The comprehension mirror. A model that misreads a word problem computes the wrong thing perfectly; free-form retrying never fixed that (bench v13: relay 0/20). Here the model DECLARES its reading — which catalog formula, which args it understood — and the server answers with the exact result PLUS a reading_check line: the substitution written out so the model can compare it against the human's sentence in plain words. The machine never claims to know the story (not_claimed is in every response); it makes the reading visible. Same engine as /api/v1/formula — the mirror cannot diverge from the math.

tools.name: date_recurrence
tools.description: Expand an RFC 5545 RRULE into dated occurrences — the closed subset, with every trap declared IN the answer. Models silently fail here: biweekly rules land every week (INTERVAL ignored: 4 of 8 dates wrong on the published demo), MONTHLY from the 31st is dropped in short months (the RFC: invalid dates MUST be ignored, never moved), mixed BYDAY like MO,2TU reads as NO dates in python-dateutil 4.0.0. Supported: FREQ DAILY/WEEKLY/MONTHLY/YEARLY, INTERVAL, COUNT xor UNTIL (both = refused by name), BYDAY with ordinals only for MONTHLY/YEARLY, BYMONTH, BYMONTHDAY signed, WKST. BYSETPOS, BYWEEKNO, BYYEARDAY, BYHOUR, BYMINUTE, BYSECOND and sub-daily FREQs are refused by name, never softly ignored. DTSTART anchors the grid and sync status is reported — rrule.js force-includes it (off-by-one), dateutil drops it silently; the RFC calls that zone UNDEFINED and we declare it. Wall-clock expansion per the RFC: DST moves the UTC instant, not the local time (per-day instants: date/tz). Cap 500 occurrences, truncation and skipped dates listed. Free, no payment.

dtstart.description: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS], ...Z, or the RFC compact 19970902T090000Z

rrule.description: RFC 5545 RRULE value; a leading 'RRULE:' is accepted and stripped

tools.name: units_shoe_size
tools.description: Shoe sizes answered in millimetres with the PUBLISHED steps as exact fractions — never one confident number. Models and charts fail here: convertisseurs print 'EU 42 -> US 9' while Nike and adidas label the SAME foot 42.5 and 42 2/3; small models invent averages ('7.5 - 1.5 = 9.5'). Inputs: foot_mm (measured) OR size+system (eu|uk|us_men|us_women|mondopoint; sizes accept 42.5, '42 2/3', '85/2'), optional width_mm for the ISO 9407 '271/100' label. Output: exact fraction position per system + the grid candidates each brand practice prints (halves and thirds are both published EU grids), steps (barleycorn 127/15 mm, Paris point 20/3 mm), the cross-system drift stated as exact numbers (per step 9/5 = 1.8 mm; 4 EU steps never equal 3 US steps), the +2 allowance declared (40/3 mm), and the foot-vs-last anchor said out loud. Brand charts stay off-contract — no brand is encoded. Out of bounds refused by name. Free, no payment.

tools.name: net_sri
tools.description: Subresource Integrity from LOCAL octets only — this tool never fetches. Give bytes_b64 or text (the exact file you reviewed) and get the ready-to-paste integrity attribute (sha256/sha384/sha512, strongest-first, W3C grammar), the crossorigin note, and full <script>/<link> tags when a url is given. Give integrity_attr to audit it: TAB/newline token separators are flagged as the CVE-2026-120423 class (a space-only verifier skips every token and accepts tampered bodies unconditionally), sha1/md5 and bad base64 refused by name, wrong-length digests caught, duplicates flagged (W3C = strongest supported wins, not all checked). URLs audited for moving parts: @latest and unversioned CDN paths flagged as planned outages, @5/@5.3 ranges as warn. With octets + attribute it VERIFIES the match locally — honest scope note included: SRI proves bytes are expected, never that they are safe. Free.

bytes_b64.description: strict base64 of the exact file bytes

integrity_attr.description: attribute to audit or verify against octets

tools.name: date_tz_ambiguity
tools.description: Does this LOCAL wall clock exist — and how many times? Give a zone and a wall clock (no offset; the offset is what is ambiguous) and get the named verdict: single (one UTC instant), fold (the wall clock happens TWICE — both instants with offset and abbreviation, PEP 495 fold rule stated), or gap (it NEVER happens — last valid and first valid wall clocks named). Transition minute, affected window and direction computed live from the installed IANA tzdata via zoneinfo — no embedded table, no fetch. Built for cron/scheduler questions the Nov 2026 incidents made concrete: K8s CronJob double-ran '30 1 * * *', cron 4.4.0 re-fired the hour AFTER the repeat, wildcard entries fire once per wall pass. Free.

local.description: wall clock with no offset: '2026-11-01 01:30' or ISO with T

tools.name: money_flight_comp
tools.description: Flight compensation (EC261 / UK261) decided by the FLIGHT DATE, not the press date: Regulation (EU) 2026/2202 applies only FROM 2027-10-23, so identical facts on two sides of that date can pay differently (the new Art. 6(4) threshold is 'EXCEEDING three hours' — exactly 180 min does not pay; the old case-law threshold was 'at least'). Give regime (EU|UK), flight_date, event (denied_boarding|cancellation|delay|missed_connection), distance_km (great circle, initial departure -> final destination, supplied), and the event numbers (delay_min; notice_days and rerouting) — get band EUR 250/400/600 or GBP 220/350/520 with the intra-Union 400 cap named, the official under-4h long-haul GBP 260 row, reductions rendered as the text states them: the carrier MAY reduce 50 % (Art. 7(2)) or 50/25 % (Art. 7(3)) — options, never silence. Table B adds the nine-month claim deadline as an EXACT date and the 30-day carrier answer duty. Zero flight fetches, zero legal promises. Free.

regime.description: never guessed — the two systems pay different money

flight_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD of the flight; selects the table version

distance_km.description: great-circle km to the FINAL destination

intra_eu.description: EU flights above 1500 km only — decides cap (b) vs (c)

extraordinary.description: carrier INVOKES extraordinary circumstances (facts assessment, not arithmetic)

tools.name: date_week
tools.description: ISO 8601 weeks, both directions, with the year-boundary trap shown on YOUR date. Pass 'date' → iso_year/iso_week/iso_day, week bounds, and the live proof of the %Y-W%V vs %G-W%V concatenation bug (formatting 2027-01-01 with the GREGORIAN year prints '2027-W53', a week that does not exist — 2027 has 52 weeks). Pass 'iso' (YYYY-Www-d) → the calendar date, nonexistent weeks REFUSED naming the theorem (a year has 53 ISO weeks iff it contains 53 Thursdays: Jan-1 Thursday, or Wednesday in a leap year — computed, zero embedded tables). Pass 'year' → weeks count, W01/W53 bounds, January days of the previous ISO year, neighbouring 53-week years. Excel/US conventions (WEEKNUM 1/2, %U, %W) rendered BESIDE ISO, never chosen for you — a German 'KW 53' and an American 'week 2' can name the same seven days. Platform notes included (PostgreSQL IYYY, Snowflake session policy, BSD strftime deviation measured in production testing). Free.

year.description: YYYY — how many weeks, does W53 exist

tools.name: money_baggage
tools.description: Cabin baggage decided by the FLIGHT DATE, not the press date. Reg. (EU) 2026/2202 applies FROM 2027-10-23: before that no EU size rule exists at all (each airline decides); from it, exactly ONE legal edge — a personal item up to 40x30x15 cm must be carried under the seat FREE. The regulation sets NO size limit for the overhead bag (The Age) and NO weight cap for the personal item; where law is silent the answer SAYS silent, it does not invent. Carrier gauges are SUPPLIED arguments (the measured 2026 table: Ryanair 40x30x20, KLM 40x30x15, easyJet 45x36x20/56x45x25…), never fetched. Fit is compared PER DIMENSION with rotation allowed — 40x18x30 passes a 40x30x20 gauge while raw-order checking fails it. The press '100 cm combined + 7 kg' reading is returned as a tested press CLAIM (the standard 55x40x20 trolley sums to 115 cm, so that reading would outlaw every normal cabin case — the law does not say it), never a rule. UK departures named out of scope. Zero fetch, not legal advice. Free.

cabin_sum_limit.description: sum limit ONLY if your carrier publishes one

tools.name: csv_excel_damage
tools.description: Before the double-click: what Excel will SILENTLY DESTROY in this CSV, per column. The damage happens ON OPEN and saving writes it back — a stripped leading zero is unrecoverable from the file (delimiter.live). Predicts Microsoft's own three Automatic Data Conversion toggles (Excel 365 2309+/16.77): leading zeros (02134->2134), text-to-date (SEPT2->2026-09-02, MARCH1->March 1 — gene names die; '3-4' is March 4 under en but April 3 under eu: SAME cell, TWO dates, so locale is an argument never a guess), the 15-significant-digit wall (4111111111111111->4111111111111110, 987654321098765432->9.87654E+17), scientific notation (1E5->100000), formula shapes (-5, +43, =... injection surface), full-width digits (１２３ compares as a different ID). A token without a year takes the CURRENT year in Excel — so as_of is REQUIRED here: determinism first. Output: per-column rule counts + samples + the prescribed import (Data>From Text/CSV typed Text, or the toggles off, or ship .xlsx). csv/fix REPAIRS after the fact; this PREDICTS before it. Detection lot — the stored-vs-displayed numFmt mask rendering (the 88 % misled study) is the queued M part. Free.

locale.description: date coercion order: en reads m/d, eu reads d/m

as_of.description: YYYY-MM-DD freezing the year Excel implies for '3/4'

tools.name: money_crossover
tools.description: Two-component tariffs (unit rate + recurring fixed): WHERE they cross, exact. The formula is published by seven web calculators that contradict each other on ROUNDING: they round the fixed delta first (19.42/0.0042 = 'about 4,623') where the exact answer is 4,623 1/3 kWh. Here Decimal never quantizes before the last step: the crossover ships as an EXACT fraction plus its decimal. DAY CONVENTIONS are named, never melted: monthly fixeds annualize by x12 exact (not 30-day months = x360), daily by x365 or a supplied 366 leap year; 'week' is REFUSED (no exact conversion). DOMINATION is a rendered answer: when one plan wins on BOTH components, 'never' comes back named with the reason. Also: equal fixeds (immediate crossover at zero), equal rates (no tradeoff), distance conversion when km per unit is SUPPLIED (EV), costs at your usage, and one-off exit/signup fees rendered as PAYBACK months — separate from the structural crossover (uktaxdrag's own distinction). Electricity, EV charging, SaaS seats, mobile data: one kernel. Zero fetch, no tariff advice. Free.

a_unit_rate.description: plan A price per unit, major units: '0.30'

a_unit_per.description: kWh / Wh / MWh, or any unit matching plan B

usage_per_period.description: your consumption to compare costs at

km_per_unit.description: supplied efficiency, e.g. '6' km/kWh → crossover in km

tools.name: csv_excel_display
tools.description: What Excel DISPLAYS from a STORED value under a numFmt code — the render, not the damage. arXiv 2611.05806 measured it: cell B9 stores 1,000,000 under '$#,##0,' (the TRAILING COMMA SCALES by a thousand) and Excel shows $1,000; six python extractors (markitdown, openpyxl, pandas, unstructured, calamine, Docling) all emit the stored value — every chat assistant and 3 of 4 coding agents tested got budget-approved numbers the human never saw. Feed the stored value (what your extractor gave you) plus the format code (styles.xml); get the display string + the rules said. Closed subset from Microsoft's OWN symbol table with its resolved examples replayed: '#.0,,' + 12200000 -> '12.2'; '(000)' + 12 -> '(012)'; '0%' + 0.5 -> '50%'; '0.00 "dollars"' + 1.23 -> '1.23 dollars'; '#.##' + 8.9 -> '8.9'; display rounding half-away-from-zero (2.5 under '0' -> 3) — and the stored value NEVER changes, only the display. Separators are SYMBOLS in the file (Microsoft states content is locale-invariant): pass the locale you display in and '1234567.891' under '#,##0.00' becomes 1.234.567,89 in de-DE. REFUSED by name: General (column-width dependent), E-notation, date/time codes, [Red], [<] conditions, * fill, _ skip, @ text. Free.

value.description: the STORED number as extracted, e.g. '1000000' or '25604.880000000001'

locale.description: display locale for separators (closed table), default en-US

tools.name: date_tz_anchor
tools.description: One wall clock, TWO clocks reading it: a naive timestamp WRITTEN against one zone (the job's/config's) and ANCHORED by a machine in another (usually a UTC box). Six production bugs measured in November 2026 share this shape: PraisonAI #4732 (naive at: silently stamped UTC, 'an hour or more off'; the fix itself used the offset in force NOW — an hour wrong across a DST change), Composio #4148 (offset + timezone both passed: event created shifted, never rejected), hermes-agent #1729, evoila/meho #2339 ('different but plausibly equivalent', 2 h in CEST), nanobot #408 (tz field never read). Feed stamp + meant_in + run_in: every candidate UTC instant, a SIGNED drift in minutes (positive = fires LATE), both wall clocks read back, single/fold/gap per zone DELEGATED to date/tz_ambiguity's engine (called, not copied). An offset in the stamp WINS (Composio's published resolution) and the naive re-anchor ships as the bug's shape, not the answer. stamped_offset replays the 'offset in force NOW' bug against the offset IN FORCE ON THAT DATE. Zones never guessed (both required for naive stamps), epoch refused by name, no clock read: the stamp IS the date. IANA via zoneinfo, past and future. Free.

meant_in.description: IANA zone the wall clock was written against (required for naive stamps)

run_in.description: IANA zone of the machine anchoring it (UTC is normal — that's the bug)

stamped_offset.description: the '+HH:MM' your code stamped at write time — audited against the offset in force on the DATE

tools.name: money_points
tools.description: What a reward point is actually worth, EXACT. cpp = (cash price - cash still paid - rewards forgone) / points x 100 — the formula six published pages agree on while contradicting on arithmetic: cardcompass prints 1.49 where the exact value is 1081/725 = 1.491034..., milesbuyer prints '13x' where 8/0.6 = 40/3. The fraction ships beside the decimal. Subtract BEFORE dividing is the trap: 450/25000 = 1.80 is what you get by FORGETTING the 35 of taxes; the answer is 83/50 = 1.66 (card-savvy's own worked example). Multi-path redemptions rank side by side (cash/gift/portal/transfer — SwitchWize's five), ties named, best/worst spread as an exact ratio. Inverted bounds are REFUSED named (min_above_max) — we do not silently sort a contract; equal bounds are a single-day window, not an error. tools.name: shop_gift_voucher
tools.description: Gift-voucher expiry DATES, jurisdiction-named, from official text replayed 24-nov-2026. IE — Consumer Protection (Gift Vouchers) Act 2019 (No. 38 of 2019), Part 4A: expiry must be 'at least 5 years from the date on which the contract was entered into' or the term is DEEMED so, and the deemed term OVERRIDES the printed one (66B(1)(b)+(c)) — a one-year print comes back PAPER_DEAD_LAW_ALIVE, the JD Sports shape (~€250,000 refunded July 2026, CCPC press 20-nov-2026). The expiry day itself still redeems: 66A(1) makes expiry 'the date AFTER which' the voucher ceases. Commencement gate 2-Dec-2019 named (CCPC business page). The euro floor ships WITH its conflict: statute '€1 or more' (66B(4)), CCPC FAQ 'more than €1' — at exactly €1.00 the statute governs, both texts travel, conflict named. Closed clash table: forced-single-use (66B(3)), voucher-count caps (66B(7)), name-mismatch fees (66B(6)), earlier replacement expiry (66B(8)) — void, non-binding, contract survives (66B(9)); the gift RECIPIENT holds all rights and the clock stays on the CONTRACT date (66B(10)). Eight exclusion classes shipped from 66A(2)(a)-(h) — loyalty, promo, return-credit (the frontier with /shop/return-deadline), utility, e-money (S.I. 183/2011)… — EXCLUDED_OUT_OF_SCOPE computes no dates. FR replayed NEGATIVE: 'no law fixes a minimum or maximum validity' — the printed date is contractual (L111-1 disclosure frames it, not its length); five-year prescription (art. 2224) has a FLOATING anchor and is carried BLOCKED, never dated; the '30 years' rumour is real-property prescription (2227) — corrected here by name. UK/BR/US refused by name, not replayed. Holiday returns are /shop/return-deadline; warranty clocks are /shop/legal-guarantee. No clock, no network, no advice. Free.

tools.name: shop_soldes_window
tools.description: French SALE WINDOWS as DATES, computed from the arrête replayed 24-nov-2026 (arrêté du 27 mai 2019, NOR ECOI1911930A, in force since 1-Jan-2020 art. 4). The grammar is CLOSED and BOTH seasons carry an advance clause: winter starts the SECOND Wednesday of January 08:00, ADVANCED to the first when that second Wednesday falls AFTER the 12th — strict, 2028-01-12 stays, 2027-01-13 moves to Jan 6 (the calendar site printing 'until Tuesday 9 February' for 2027 applied the clause's absence: the pain caught in the act). Summer starts the LAST Wednesday of June 08:00, moved back to the penultimate when the last falls after the 28th — so été 2027 opens June 23, not June 30. Duration is art. 3: four weeks, the start day COUNTED (end = start + 27, verified against four official vectors). Then the part no calendar site carries: SEVEN annual derogations, each shipped with its verbatim and its JORF — été 2020 fixed to Wed 15 July (arrêté 10-juin-2020, also named for 06/2A/2B/66); winter 2021 fixed to Wed 20 January (arrêté 23-déc-2020, + 54/55/57/88/971) then PORTÉE À SIX SEMAINES (arrêté 15-févr-2021 — 20 janv -> 2 mars; La Réunion, Saint-Barthélemy and Saint-Martin EXCLUDED by name, four weeks); été 2021 fixed to 30 June — with MOSSELLE alone at 26 June (arrêté 15-juin-2021, the line no press table copies); Guadeloupe été 2021 moved to Thursday 7 October (arrêté 23-sept-2021); été 2023 and été 2026 CARRIED TO FIVE WEEKS (arrêtés 6-juill-2023, 3-juill-2026 — canicule; service-public A15000: 'devaient se terminer le 21 juillet [...] jusqu'au mardi 28 juillet'), scoped by PREDICATE on the text, not by memory: 2026 counts départements whose date comes from Article 1, which is why Moselle's SUMMER gets five weeks while Corsica keeps four. The annex is VERSIONED: the 21-avril-2023 arrêté (in force 17 May 2023) removed rows 06, 66, 973 — windows beginning before it keep the initial line (Perpignan été 2022 July 6; guyane hiver 2023 Jan 4), after it the common rule (moneyvox's 'Guyane 5 October 2023' recycled an ABROGATED line — the press artifact this tool exists to refuse). East-4 départements open 'premier jour ouvré' — the word is undefined: strict OUVRÉ (Mon-Fri, 1er excluded) is first, the OUVRABLE reading (Saturday counts, what tpeactu/france.fr print) travels as a NAMED conflict only when the two dates differ — which is 2027 (Jan 2 vs Jan 4), not every year. Saint-Pierre counts 'premier mercredi APRÈS le 15 janvier' — after STRICT: 2025-01-15 IS the Wednesday, so the window opens the 22nd. Territory is the CLOSED annex table (codes, names, cities, 'lorraine', 'corse' fan out); foreign calendars — Belgium, Luxembourg, Switzerland, Quebec, UK — are REFUSED BY NAME: this table replays only the French arrêté and lends dates no memory. Years before 2020 are refused with art. 4 verbatim. as_of is an argument: 'Dans 43 jours' is arithmetic, not a clock. No network, no wall clock, no shopping advice. Free.

tools.description: Belgian SALE WINDOWS as DATES, computed from art. The clauses are Dated, not remembered: winter 2016 opened Saturday 2 January (press replayed), winter 2027 opens the same way — and the SPF names the one-month standstill 'du 2 décembre au 1er janvier' while some press still prints 3 December: the next-day boundary, caught in the act. Then the two corona years, each with its verbatim and Moniteur numac: été 2020 moved to 1-31 August (loi 27-mai-2020, art. 4); winter 2021 REPORTED to Monday 4 January (AR 10-déc-2020: no Saturday crowd opening — the Sunday clause FIRED but was OVERRULED, and both facts travel) then PROLONGED to 15 February by a LOI (02-févr-2021 — the King was capped at one month by § 2; press titles said 14 February, the adopted text says 15, the conflict is dated). Eligibility (30 days on sale, still held at the start), the sectoral ban (habillement/maroquinerie/chaussures, no announced cuts or discount titles during the wait), the braderie exception (≤ 4 days, § 4) and the liquidation escape (§ 5) ride the answer as verbatim. The 20-May-2026 Conseil d'État annulments are carried as a NAMED conflict — the tool dates, it does not plead. Gate: Livre VI only (≤ 2014 winters refused with the 1991-law facts); France is refused by name pointing at /shop/soldes-window; Luxembourg is refused by name — its dates are DATED BY ACT and live on their own card: /shop/soldes-lu — no formula, no invented date. as_of is an argument. No network, free.

tools.description: Luxembourg SALE WINDOWS as DATES from the ACTES themselves — the law of 23-Dec-2016 art. 1 § 4 says a règlement grand-ducal fixes the opening and closing dates EVERY YEAR: no second-Wednesday rule, no Sunday clause, no formula. A-928); the 2023 one fixes the BOUNDARY itself ('samedi, le 23 juillet 2023' was a Sunday — the Official Journal printed a false end, the rectification A-96 says Saturday 22 July: the press and the government communique had said 22 from the start, so quoting A-511 without A-96 contradicts the State). The one-month cap rides as a VERIFIED invariant: no replayed period exceeds 30 days.
